chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me: Yaqoob ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, from Mu'az ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Be patient with the enemies of the blessings, for you cannot treat those who disobey God regarding yourself any better than by obeying God regarding them.
ai.seo_question: How should one respond to enemies of blessings according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) defines the 'enemies of blessings' as those who hinder divine favors, advising believers to counter their hostility not with retaliation, but with steadfast obedience to God. This approach transforms spiritual adversity into a means of elevating one's rank, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *sabr* (patience) as an active, worshipful state rather than passive endurance. The narration underscores that maintaining divine servitude amidst external opposition is the highest form of recompense.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 1-71 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted on the authority of Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Muawiyah ibn Wahab, on the authority of Mu’az ibn Muslim that Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) said, “
Be patient with the enemies of the blessings . You cannot treat those who disobey God regarding yourself any better than by obeying God regarding them.”
